es: Distinguir en un texto de estudio la afirmación (claim), la prueba (evidence) y la opinión, juzgar si una prueba es sólida o solo anecdótica y reconocer las expresiones que señalan cada función.

vocabulary.es: pruebas, datos que apoyan una idea
anecdótico, basado en un caso aislado

teaching.en: A claim is an idea the writer defends, and it stays weak until the writer can back up the claim with evidence.
teaching.es: Una afirmación es una idea que el autor defiende, y sigue siendo débil hasta que el autor puede respaldarla con pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim es lo que se defiende; evidence es lo que lo apoya. Back up + objeto + with + prueba.
segments: A claim is an idea the writer defends, and it stays
weak until the writer can back up the claim with evidence.
teaching.audioText: A claim is an idea the writer defends, and it stays weak until the writer can back up the claim with evidence.

teaching.en: According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours, which is the kind of data that supports the claim.
teaching.es: Según una encuesta a 300 estudiantes, la mayoría duerme menos de siete horas, que es el tipo de datos que apoya la afirmación.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + fuente señala una prueba. Una survey y sus data se pueden comprobar.
segments: According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under
seven hours, which is the kind of data that supports the claim.
teaching.audioText: According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours, which is the kind of data that supports the claim.

teaching.en: Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep, but what they argue is a claim, not a fact, until it has been tested.
teaching.es: Algunos expertos sostienen que los adolescentes necesitan dormir más, pero lo que sostienen es una afirmación, no un hecho, hasta que se ponga a prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Argue that introduce la tesis de alguien. Un fact se puede comprobar; una afirmación aún debe probarse.
segments: Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep, but what they argue
is a claim, not a fact, until it has been tested.
teaching.audioText: Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep, but what they argue is a claim, not a fact, until it has been tested.

teaching.en: In my opinion, mornings are far too early for teenagers, but an opinion says what someone feels and cannot be checked like a fact.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, las mañanas son demasiado tempranas para los adolescentes, pero una opinión dice lo que alguien siente y no se puede comprobar como un hecho.
teaching.explanationEs: In my opinion y I feel that señalan una opinión: es válida, pero no cuenta como prueba.
segments: In my opinion, mornings are far too early for teenagers, but an
opinion says what someone feels and cannot be checked like a fact.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion, mornings are far too early for teenagers, but an opinion says what someone feels and cannot be checked like a fact.

teaching.en: A single story about one tired student is anecdotal, so it cannot back up a general claim the way a large survey can.
teaching.es: La historia de un solo estudiante cansado es anecdótica, así que no puede respaldar una afirmación general como lo hace una encuesta grande.
teaching.explanationEs: Anecdotal describe un caso aislado: ilustra una idea, pero no la demuestra.
segments: A single story about one tired student is anecdotal, so it cannot
back up a general claim the way a large survey can.
teaching.audioText: A single story about one tired student is anecdotal, so it cannot back up a general claim the way a large survey can.

teaching.en: Writers who assert a sweeping claim, such as «all teenagers are lazy», should name a credible source, because a confident tone is not evidence.
teaching.es: Quienes afirman algo tan general como «todos los adolescentes son vagos» deberían nombrar una fuente creíble, porque un tono seguro no es una prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Assert suena rotundo; sweeping describe una afirmación demasiado general; credible valora la fuente. La seguridad del tono no sustituye a las pruebas.
segments: Writers who assert a sweeping claim, such as «all teenagers are lazy»,
should name a credible source, because a confident tone is not evidence.
teaching.audioText: Writers who assert a sweeping claim, such as «all teenagers are lazy», should name a credible source, because a confident tone is not evidence.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué función cumple la segunda oración?

choices.text: Evidence: it gives a source and a figure that can be checked.
Claim: it states the main idea that the writer wants to defend.
Opinion: it says how the writer feels about early mornings.

feedback.es: La segunda oración cita una fuente (una encuesta) y una cifra comprobable: es la prueba que respalda la afirmación de la primera.

hint.es: Fíjate en la fuente y en la cifra: son lo que se puede comprobar.

origin.text: Schools should start at nine. According to a survey of 300 students, 68 percent sleep under seven hours on school nights.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según una encuesta a 300 estudiantes, la mayoría duerme poco.»

feedback.es: According to + fuente introduce una prueba y deja claro de dónde sale el dato.

hint.es: Es la palabra que, junto a to, introduce una fuente.

origin.text: Teenagers need more sleep, and, ___ to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En mi opinión, las mañanas son demasiado pronto para los adolescentes.»

answer.text: In my opinion mornings are too early for teenagers

feedback.es: In my opinion abre una valoración personal, que no cuenta como prueba.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula que señala una opinión.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige qué dato funciona como prueba en el argumento.

choices.text: Her sister's tiredness at eight o'clock in the morning on school days.
The survey of three hundred students who slept under seven hours.
Her view that nine o'clock would be the best start.

feedback.es: La encuesta aporta una fuente y un dato comprobable; la hermana es un caso aislado (anecdótico) y las nueve como hora ideal es una opinión.

origin.audio: In this week's study skills podcast, the host reads out a short argument. Schools, she says, should start later in the morning. To back up that claim, she quotes a survey of three hundred students, most of whom slept under seven hours on school nights. She then adds that, in her own opinion, nine o'clock would be the best time, and that her sister is always exhausted at eight. The host admits that the last detail is only anecdotal, but she thinks the survey is credible.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada oración con la función que cumple en el texto.

pairs: A survey of 500 workers found that 40 percent felt tired.
Workers should be allowed to start later.
I feel that early meetings are a bad idea.
My cousin is always tired at eight.

feedback.es: La encuesta es una prueba; «should» marca la afirmación; «I feel» marca una opinión; el primo es un caso aislado, es decir, una anécdota.

pairs: A survey of 500 workers found that 40 percent felt tired.
Workers should be allowed to start later.
I feel that early meetings are a bad idea.
My cousin is always tired at eight.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Por qué la tercera oración no sirve como prueba?

choices.text: It repeats the claim in other words without a source.
It gives a fact about the building, but no source.
It reports a personal feeling that nobody can check.

feedback.es: «Personally, I find…» expresa una sensación personal que nadie puede comprobar; la prueba es la segunda oración, con una cifra atribuida al personal.

origin.text: The council should close the library on Sundays. Library staff say that fewer than ten people visit on Sundays. Personally, I find the building cold and dark.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué parte del artículo es la prueba más sólida.

choices.text: The teachers' report linking less homework to lower stress.
The story of her cousin, who now smiles more than before.
Her final comment that homework is a waste of time.

feedback.es: El informe de los profesores aporta datos de muchos alumnos; el primo es un caso aislado y la última frase es una opinión.

origin.audio: A student wrote in the school newspaper that homework should be banned. She claims that pupils who do no homework are happier, and as proof she mentions her cousin, who stopped doing homework last year and now smiles more. Later, she quotes a report from a group of teachers, which found that pupils with less homework reported lower stress. She ends by saying that homework is a waste of time. The editor added a note: the report is credible, but the cousin is only one case.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué da a entender la nota del editor?

choices.text: That the whole article is unreliable and should be ignored.
That only part of the evidence should be taken seriously.
That the student's claim has now been proven correct.

feedback.es: El editor separa lo creíble (el informe) de lo que es solo un caso (el primo): da a entender que una parte de las pruebas pesa más que la otra.

origin.audio: A student wrote in the school newspaper that homework should be banned. She claims that pupils who do no homework are happier, and as proof she mentions her cousin, who stopped doing homework last year and now smiles more. Later, she quotes a report from a group of teachers, which found that pupils with less homework reported lower stress. She ends by saying that homework is a waste of time. The editor added a note: the report is credible, but the cousin is only one case.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hace una afirmación fuerte, pero no puede respaldarla con cifras.»

feedback.es: Back up es el verbo frasal para respaldar una afirmación con pruebas; sin cifras ni fuente, la afirmación queda sin apoyo.

origin.text: The writer makes a bold claim about school uniforms, but she has not given a single figure or source, so she cannot ___ it up.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función cumple «A study of twelve schools found no difference…»?

choices.text: It is a claim that repeats the experts' view.
It is an opinion that supports the experts.
It is evidence that goes against the experts' claim.

feedback.es: El estudio aporta datos comprobables y contradicen la afirmación de los expertos: es una prueba en contra, no una opinión ni una repetición de la tesis.

origin.text: Some experts argue that uniforms improve behaviour in class. A study of twelve schools found no difference in behaviour between schools with and without uniforms. In my view, however, uniforms are a good idea.

prompt.es: Escucha. ¿Por qué solo la tercera reseña ayuda a decidir?

choices.text: Because it offers facts that the reader can check.
Because it is the most positive of the three reviews.
Because it comes from the person who owns the café.

feedback.es: Las dos primeras reseñas son opiniones; la tercera da precios concretos, que son datos comprobables y sirven para decidir.

origin.audio: I have read three reviews of the new café. One calls it the best coffee in town, another says that it is far too expensive, and the third gives the price of every drink on the menu. Only the third can really help me decide.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender «However, the survey did not ask about age»?

choices.text: That cycling to work has no health benefits at all.
That the evidence is weaker than it first looks.
That the survey of 2,000 commuters was badly written.

feedback.es: «However…» introduce una reserva: sin datos sobre la edad o la forma física, los ciclistas podrían ser simplemente más sanos; la prueba pesa menos de lo que parecía.

origin.text: Many people say that cycling to work is healthier than driving. A survey of 2,000 commuters found that cyclists take fewer sick days. However, the survey did not ask about age or health.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una afirmación sin pruebas es solo una opinión.»

answer.text: A claim without evidence is only an opinion

feedback.es: Sin datos ni fuente que la respalden, una afirmación no pasa de ser una opinión.
